title: cuda-graph: add shape-guarded capture/replay warmup to avoid replay regressions
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: recent rollout of cuda-graph capture/replay (see pr-18345 pr-18712 pr-19458) produced a set of subtle latency regressions for inputs that change token lengths frequently. Root cause: captured graphs were being replayed for inputs with different runtime shapes which caused extra kernel fallbacks and deoptimized code paths (KV cache alignment and attention kernel edge cases). This PR introduces a conservative shape-guarding and warmup flow for capture/replay to avoid replaying invalid graphs and to ensure graphs are captured on representative shapes. The change includes: 1) shape guard metadata attached to graph objects (max_seq, batch_dim, kv_length_bucket) recorded as simple tags; 2) pre-capture warmup that synthesizes a small number of representative batch/sequence shapes drawn from recent traffic distribution; 3) runtime checks that fall back to the JIT path when an incoming request doesn't match the graph's guards; 4) a lightweight eviction policy that retires graphs that are never reused to limit memory pressure; 5) telemetry and traces to detect mismatch rates and warmup effectiveness. Backwards compatibility: when graphs are absent we still run the existing eager/JIT path. Rollout plan: gated rollout on canary nodes (10% traffic) with a telemetry gate (mismatch_rate < 0.5% over 24h) before full rollout. See linked Linear ENG-2314 and ENG-2467 for performance targets and monitoring dashboards. Checklist: - [x] implement shape guard recording - [x] implement warmup synthesis using traffic histogram - [x] add runtime guard/fallback path - [x] add eviction and memory accounting - [x] add unit + integration tests - [x] add e2e perf benchmark in perf-canary Results: on our canary tests with long-tail sequence distributions the change eliminates the 5-15% p95 tail regressions previously observed and reduces graph mismatch fallbacks from ~6% to ~0.4% (numbers on a 8xA100 testbed). Related: pr-18345 pr-18712 pr-19023 pr-19458.

review_comments: Ethan Ruelas: Overall looks good. A few nits on naming and a question about the eviction threshold default (30m) - can we make it configurable via runtime flags?
Priya Menon: replied: made eviction timeout configurable via runtime config + exposed a debug endpoint to force eviction for tests.
Maya Chen: Please add a stress test for repeated short/long sequence alternation; saw a flaky case in perf-canary where mismatch_rate spiked under synthetic alternation.
Priya Menon: added stress test and fixed a race in the warmup sampler that could undercount bucket hits.
release_notes: Add conservative shape guards and warmup for CUDA graph capture/replay to avoid replay-induced latency regressions; warmup synthesis and eviction policy included.
